issues.description: Method visibility mismatch for helper method singFarmSongVerse(Animal): the problem statement's textual instructions explicitly ask students to implement singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) as public (problem statement text), while the UML in the problem statement and both the template and the solution declare/implement the helper as private. Specifically: (1) problem statement text requests a public helper (problem_statement.md lines 112-116); (2) problem statement UML shows singFarmSongVerse as private (problem_statement.md line 19); (3) template Farm.java declares the method as private (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, signature at line 18); (4) solution Farm.java declares the method as private (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, signature at line 33). This contradiction is not a pedagogical TODO — it gives conflicting requirements about the method's access level and can confuse students about what signature/visibility their implementation and tests should use.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the visibility contradiction so students have a single clear requirement. Two reasonable fixes: (A) Update the problem statement text to remove or change the sentence requesting a public helper and state that singFarmSongVerse should be private (matching UML, template, and solution). OR (B) Change the template and solution Farm.java method signature to public (public void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) and update any tests/examples that rely on visibility. Ensure the UML, code comments, and textual instructions are consistent after the change.
